title: Setting history straight; music from his mother's singing
summary: He wants to attend a jazz convention to correct history; his first memory is his mother singing and his father was a railroad chef.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Another thing that J. C. has reiterated time and time again, and that is an ambition to get himself in shape, get to one of those jazz conventions and let them get their say out, especially their incorrect information in history, to stand up and tell them how it really was. And he really rolls the "really."

I asked him how he really got started with music and his answer was, "I always had music, even in the very beginning. My mother sang to me. That's the first thing I remember." His father, by the way, was a chef on the railroads. From the very beginning, music was the most important thing in the universe to J. C., and he has mentioned this several times.
